content: It seems that Claude Code (coupled with one existing Lean MCP tool and a few context files) is already a powerful autoformalization agent that everyone can use! I did an experiment: https://github.com/bridgekat/claude-formalizer
(with a few sub-agents running in parallel, this completes in ~8 hours)

When I was still an undergrad, I always wanted to make an automated theorem prover or autoformalizer so I can easily consolidate and verify my mathematical knowledge (in a way that might be actually useful). I was trying to follow a more conventional approach (learning type theory and proof theory, designing and optimizing brute-force search) and even thinking about doing a PhD. Yet it seems now that all human-crafted systems and heuristics look pale in comparison to LLMs trained on huge amounts of data (in any case, if current LLM-generated proofs are considered low quality, then so are those produced by brute-force search methods), so I am not sure what to do next

This one was already done by the Beijing team https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583339-AI-authored-projects/topic/Archon.3A.20Auto-Formalization.20of.20FirstProof.20Problems.204.20.26.206/near/577156272 and their proof is on the public internet. Can you be sure that Claude didn't just copy it?

How much did it cost to get Claude to generate this solution?

Did you run a tool like comparator to check that the AI solution didn't have cheats in it?

Kevin Buzzard said:

This was not actually an unattended run. I observed the process, and that includes every tool call it used.

  1. Although I did not ban Web Search, it only uses the internet to find existing Mathlib components and reported that significant parts haven't been formalized yet (apparently unaware of Archon's formalization); then it goes on planning their formalization on its own. It never use Web Search again after this point - only Loogle and LeanSearch. (You can try running the same configuration yourself!)
  2. I was running on Claude Max 5x subscription, which is much cheaper than the API. I can only see it hitting 40% of monthly limit. Based on a recent estimate, this would correspond to $600 in API pricing. (Not an exact number - unfortunately Claude's subscription plans are not completely transparent.)

The solution produced is slightly shorter than the Archon's solution (1850 LoC vs. 2300 LoC), but this may be due to poorer organization (longer proofs per lemma and fewer lemmas) and the direct use of Mathlib lapMatrix in the theorem statement (Archon formalized its own version of graph Laplacian and then proved equivalence with the Mathlib version).
I believe the numbers (total time and cost) roughly match those provided by the Archon team.

While filling in the proof, the agents exhibited a reasonable work pattern: experiment with Mathlib definitions or construct pieces of proofs in temporary Lean files -> replace a sorry with a chunk of proof (possibly containing smaller sorrys) -> run Lean MCP tool to check for errors -> look up contexts at error locations -> fix errors in small batches until none left -> repeat. At least they seem to be doing real work and trial-and-error.

I have also checked the statements (final theorem and intermediate lemmas) and they indeed match the DetailedProof.tex draft, which in turn matches the original informal proof.
